snarl verb

also growl, grrr, grr, growl (of a dog)

classical

Traupman 142
Ter. Phorm. 341: ille ringitur, tū rīdeās
Traupman 324

ringī

Other words

  • err — grrr, a dog’s snarl

    interjection · also used · Renaissance · Comen. OP Alph.: Canis ringitur, under R; Pers. 1.109 (Lewis & Short s.v. canīnus): littera canīna, the letter R

    The snarl as Comenius spells it in his animal alphabet (1658); Persius already calls R the dog’s letter.

  • fremō, fremere, fremuī, fremitum — growl, of dogs and big cats

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Lucr. 5.1064 (Lewis & Short s.v. fremō): mollia ricta fremunt, of angry Molossian hounds; Traupman 145, of tigers

Examples

  • Canis ringitur.

    The dog snarls (R, err, in the animal alphabet).Comen. OP Alph.

See also dog, roar.

SourcesLewis & Short: ringor · Lewis & Short: fremo · Lewis & Short: caninus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 142, 145, 324.

Comenius from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-comenius).
